rationale:
Issue #532 describes a pre-existing non-termination/stack overflow in _sortByDependents: a no-env dependency waits on an env-specific implementation whose own dependency is registered in a parent package and therefore never enters the sorted set, so recursion never makes progress. The minimized production patch is a single hunk in injectable_generator/lib/code_builder/builder_utils.dart that changes exactly that env loop, treating a dependency absent from both unSorted and sorted (i.e., external/unregistered) as non-blocking instead of returning false. The trigger test 'should terminate sorting when a no-env dependency waits on an unsortable env variant' rebuilds the reported shape directly (env-scoped Service impl depending on unregistered ExternalDependency, a second env-scoped Service impl, and a no-env Consumer depending on Service), asserts via lookupDependency that ExternalDependency is unregistered, then requires sortDependencies to terminate with both Service variants before Consumer. It uses only pre-existing helpers (DependencyConfig.factory, InjectedDependency, ImportableType, lookupDependency, sortDependencies); the patch adds no new production API, so the trigger does not depend on the fix's surface. Strict evidence (both original and post-minimization) reports build passing on both revisions, a unique declared selector failing alone on the buggy revision, deterministic reproduction across 3 repetitions with 3 fingerprint groups, buggy full-suite failures limited to the reproduced trigger, and all fixed isolated/suite/reversed runs green. No unrelated refactor, formatting, docs, or config change appears in the minimized patch; the only added comment documents the new condition. active_same_project_root_causes is empty and the root cause matches the single allowed verified issue key.

Issue #532 reports a stack overflow in `_sortByDependents` when a no-env dependency waits on a type that has multiple environment-specific registrations, one of which depends on an external/unregistered type that can never enter `sorted`, producing endless recursion. The minimized production patch touches exactly that env loop in injectable_generator/lib/code_builder/builder_utils.dart, adding a single condition that treats a dependency absent from both `unSorted` and `sorted` (i.e. external/unregistered, resolved by a parent package) as non-blocking, plus an explanatory comment. That is precisely the causal chain described in the issue body, and no refactor, rename, feature extension, config, or doc change accompanies it: one hunk, 7 additions / 3 deletions, one production file. The trigger is the unchanged upstream test from the same fixing commit; it builds the reported shape directly (no-env `Consumer` -> `Service` with `prod` impl depending on unregistered `ExternalDependency` and a separate `dev` impl), asserts via `lookupDependency` that the external type is genuinely unregistered, then requires `sortDependencies` to terminate with the env variants ordered before the consumer. It exercises only pre-existing APIs (`sortDependencies`, `lookupDependency`, `DependencyConfig.factory`, `InjectedDependency`, `ImportableType`); the fix introduces no new production API, so no post-fix surface is relied upon. Strict machine evidence on the post-minimization state passes every gate: build on both revisions, isolated buggy differential on the single declared selector, deterministic fingerprints across 3 repetitions, fixed-side isolated/suite/reversed all green, and buggy full-suite failures limited to the reproduced trigger. `active_same_project_root_causes` is empty and the proposed key matches the sole entry in `allowed_root_cause_ids`, so the root cause is not a duplicate.

risks: Metadata inconsistency: source_candidate.approved_trigger_selectors names an unrelated pre-existing test ('should handle factory params in dependency chain') while the validated selector is the new regression test; the strict gates and trigger_tests agree on the regression test, so the approved-selector field appears stale.
source_candidate.commit_stats reports test_dart_file_count=0 / other_file_count=1 even though the changed test file is a Dart test; classification noise only, the patch content is unambiguous.

The trigger reproduces the defect at the sorting-unit level rather than through a full multi-package build_runner run, so the analyzer-9.0.0-specific conditions mentioned in the issue are not exercised end to end.
The fix silently treats any dependency missing from both sets as externally provided, which could mask genuinely missing registrations; this behavioral tradeoff is not covered by the trigger.

risks: Screening metadata is internally inconsistent: `approved_trigger_selectors` names 'should handle factory params in dependency chain', while the validated and declared trigger is 'should terminate sorting when a no-env dependency waits on an unsortable env variant'. The strict gates bind to the latter, but the selector approval record should be reconciled.

The trigger exercises `sortDependencies` at unit level rather than reproducing the original end-to-end `build_runner` stack overflow, so the reported symptom is reproduced through its proven mechanism rather than the user-facing failure mode.

The buggy-side failure of a non-terminating sort can surface as stack exhaustion, which is sensitive to VM stack limits; determinism held across 3 repetitions here but is environment-dependent in principle.

The fix treats any dependency missing from both sets as externally satisfied, which also masks genuine typos or truly unregistered types in the env-specific path; that behavioral widening is intended by the maintainers but is not covered by the trigger.
No analyzer-clean requirement was enforced (`require_analyze_clean` false), so static diagnostics on either revision are unverified.
